entries.name: 100 Black Men of America
entries.description: National organization of Black men dedicated to mentorship, education, economic empowerment, and health for Black youth and communities. Founded in New York City in 1963; the Atlanta chapter (founded 1986) became the flagship model for the national federation. Roughly 100 chapters across the US, each with adult-mentorship and youth-mentorship programs. Membership is open to Black men committed to the organization's mission and mentorship work.

entries.name: National 4-H Council
entries.description: Largest US youth-development organization, founded around 1902 and now operated through the Cooperative Extension System of US land-grant universities. Approximately 6 million youth members ages 5–19. Programs cover agriculture, science, healthy living, and leadership through the "Head, Heart, Hands, Health" framework. Adult volunteer leaders provide significant mentorship — many adult men in rural agricultural communities maintain their 4-H involvement across generations.

entries.name: 611 Bread of Life Christian Church Men's Ministry
entries.description: Men's-ministry network of 611 Bread of Life Christian Church (六一一靈糧堂), one of Hong Kong's largest Pentecostal/charismatic megachurches, founded 2001. Operates men's small groups, retreats, and the men-specific "Manhood" formation tracks. Cantonese-medium primarily with some English-medium content. Distinctive Cantonese-charismatic register reaches local-language men's audiences that Anglo-Anglican and English-medium ministries don't.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Bahamas
entries.description: Bahamas AA service body, coordinating English-language meetings primarily in Nassau (Providence Island) and modest meetings on the Family Islands. Standard 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly. Meetings serve a mix of Bahamian, expatriate, and tourist-area populations.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Barbados
entries.description: Barbados AA service body, coordinating English-language meetings primarily in Bridgetown and the south coast. Standard 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly. Meetings serve a mix of Bajan, expatriate, and tourist-area populations.

entries.name: AA en Español (Alcohólicos Anónimos en Español)
entries.description: Spanish-language meetings of Alcoholics Anonymous across the United States. Same fellowship structure as English-language AA — Twelve Steps, Twelve Traditions, anonymous, free, peer-led — with Spanish-speaking groups (Grupos Hispanos) and Spanish-language resources. Densest in California, Texas, Florida, New York, and Illinois. Many cities have dedicated Spanish-language intergroups; aa.org/es is the central Spanish-language landing page.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Ghana
entries.description: Ghanaian General Service Office of Alcoholics Anonymous, coordinating AA meetings primarily in Accra, Kumasi, and Takoradi. Standard AA 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly, English-language. Meeting density is modest — Ghana's AA infrastructure is smaller than Nigeria's or South Africa's but stable.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Hong Kong
entries.description: Hong Kong's AA service body, coordinating English- and Cantonese-language meetings across HK Island, Kowloon, and the New Territories. AA arrived in Hong Kong in the late 1950s. Standard 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly. Expatriate-heavy English meeting density is one of the highest in Asia given Hong Kong's professional / financial-services demographics.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous India
entries.description: General Service Office of Alcoholics Anonymous India, coordinating thousands of AA meetings across India. AA reached India in the late 1950s; the General Service Office is based in Hyderabad. Standard AA 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly, in English, Hindi, and many regional languages. Densest in major metros (Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata) and growing rapidly in tier-2 cities.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Jamaica
entries.description: Jamaican AA service body, coordinating meetings primarily in Kingston, Montego Bay, Mandeville, and Ocho Rios. Standard AA 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly, English-language. Meeting density is modest given Jamaica's scale; meetings serve a mix of local Jamaican and expatriate / tourist-area populations.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Kenya
entries.description: Kenyan General Service Office of Alcoholics Anonymous, coordinating AA meetings across major Kenyan metros — Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru, Eldoret. Standard AA 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly. Meetings are predominantly English-language with growing Kiswahili meetings.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Malaysia
entries.description: Malaysia's AA service body, coordinating English-language meetings primarily in Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Johor Bahru, Kuching, and Kota Kinabalu. Standard 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly. Meetings are predominantly English-language given AA's expat-and-middle-class-Malaysian base.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Nigeria
entries.description: Nigerian General Service Office of Alcoholics Anonymous, coordinating AA meetings across major Nigerian metros — Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Ibadan, Kano. Standard AA 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly, English-language. Meeting density is modest given Nigeria's scale but the network is established. Meetings serve both Nigerian and expatriate participants.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Philippines
entries.description: Philippines AA service body, coordinating meetings primarily in Metro Manila, Cebu, Davao, Baguio, Subic, and several other major cities, plus an active online network. Standard 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly. Meetings are predominantly English-language (with Tagalog and Cebuano alternatives growing). The Philippines has a substantial AA infrastructure relative to many Asian countries — both expat-driven and local-Filipino-driven.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Singapore
entries.description: Singapore's General Service Office of Alcoholics Anonymous, coordinating English-language AA meetings across the city-state. Standard AA 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly, open or closed format depending on the meeting. Meetings are predominantly English-language and serve a mix of local Singaporean and expatriate populations. Meeting density is modest in absolute terms but stable.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous South Africa
entries.description: South African General Service Office of Alcoholics Anonymous, coordinating roughly 700+ AA meetings across the country — primarily in English, Afrikaans, and isiZulu, with regional language support. AA arrived in South Africa in 1946. Standard AA 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly, open or closed format depending on the meeting. Densest in Gauteng and Western Cape.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Trinidad and Tobago
entries.description: Trinidad and Tobago AA service body, coordinating English-language meetings primarily in Port of Spain, San Fernando, and on Tobago. Standard 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly. Meetings serve a mix of Trinidadian, Tobagonian, expatriate, and visiting populations.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous United Arab Emirates
entries.description: UAE AA service body, coordinating English-language meetings primarily in Dubai (densest), Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, and a growing online network. AA reached the UAE in the late 1980s alongside the expansion of Western expatriate professional populations. Standard 12-step format: free, anonymous, weekly. Almost all meetings are English-language given expat demographics. Meetings typically held in licensed religious-compound venues (St Mary's Catholic, Holy Trinity Anglican, etc.) given UAE's regulatory framework.

entries.name: Acts 29 Network
entries.description: Reformed evangelical church-planting network founded in 2000, focused on supporting and assessing church-planters across the US and globally. Member churches typically run distinctive men's-ministry programming with Reformed theological framing — emphasizing biblical manhood, accountability, and intentional discipleship. Active across the US with concentration in major metros.

entries.name: Adult Children of Alcoholics & Dysfunctional Families (ACA)
entries.description: 12-step fellowship for adults raised in alcoholic, abusive, or otherwise dysfunctional family systems, founded in 1978. Meetings address how childhood patterns shape adult relationships, work, and self-perception, using the program's "Laundry List" of common traits as a starting point. Phone, online, and in-person meetings nationally; free, anonymous, peer-led.

entries.name: Adventist Men's Ministries
entries.description: Men's ministry department of the Seventh-day Adventist Church (SDA), with chapters at member SDA congregations across the US. Local groups run study, service, retreats, and an annual men's congress at the conference and union levels. The SDA's distinctive theology — Saturday Sabbath worship, vegetarian-leaning health emphasis, end-times eschatology — shapes the men's ministry's character distinctly from mainline or evangelical Protestant counterparts.

entries.name: AHEPA (American Hellenic Educational Progressive Association)
entries.description: Greek-American fraternal organization founded in 1922 in Atlanta, originally to combat anti-Greek discrimination (notably Ku Klux Klan attacks on Greek-American immigrants). Now broadly serves the Greek-American community with chapters across the US. Programs include Hellenic cultural preservation, scholarships, and charitable work. While not formally Greek-Orthodox, the organization is deeply intertwined with Greek-Orthodox Church communities.

entries.name: Alcoholics Anonymous
entries.description: International fellowship of men and women recovering from alcoholism, founded in 1935. Meetings happen multiple times daily in most US cities; many groups host men-only formats. Free, anonymous, and the lowest-barrier intake of any recovery community — a foundational door for any man in active crisis around drinking.

entries.name: Aleph Society
entries.description: Jewish educational organization founded in 1988 to support the work of Rabbi Adin Even-Israel Steinsaltz (1937–2020), focusing on making Talmud study accessible to broad Jewish audiences. While not strictly a men's organization, Aleph Society partners support Talmud-study chevrutas (study pairs) and small-group classes that traditionally have a strong men's-participation register in Orthodox communities.

entries.name: All Pro Dad
entries.description: National fatherhood organization running "All Pro Dad's Day" — monthly father-child breakfasts at participating elementary schools across the US. Founded in 1997 as a program of Family First (a Christian family-policy organization in Tampa, FL). The school-based programming is religion-dry by design, focused on the dad-child relationship and structured conversation. Workplace and community-chapter formats also exist. Free for participants.

entries.name: Alpine Club of Canada (ACC)
entries.description: Canada's national climbing and mountaineering organization, founded in 1906 in Winnipeg. Operates a network of mountain huts across the Canadian Rockies, regional sections, courses, and expeditions. Mixed-gender by design; men's-gathering function emerges through climbing partnerships, expedition cohorts, and section events.

entries.name: AME Sons of Allen
entries.description: Men's ministry of the African Methodist Episcopal Church (AME), known as Sons of Allen after Richard Allen, the AME's founder (1816). Local Sons of Allen chapters at member AME congregations run breakfasts, study groups, service projects, and an annual congress. The AME Church is the oldest independent Black Protestant denomination in the US.

entries.name: AME Zion Men's Ministry
entries.description: Men's ministry of the African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church (AME Zion), founded as a denomination in 1796 in New York City. Distinct from the AME Church (founded 1816 in Philadelphia), with its own structure and history — notable for Frederick Douglass and Sojourner Truth's affiliations and its abolition-era role as the "Freedom Church." Local men's groups at member congregations across the US.

entries.name: American Alpine Club
entries.description: Climbing and mountaineering organization founded in 1902, with national HQ in Golden, CO and approximately 30 regional sections across the US. Members get access to lodge facilities (notably the New River Gorge Climbers' Campground), climbing-grant programs, the AAC library, and section-based events. Mixed-gender by design; men's-gathering function emerges through climbing partnerships, expedition cohorts, and section events.

entries.name: American Group Psychotherapy Association
entries.description: National professional association for group psychotherapists, founded in 1942. AGPA's website hosts a "Find a Therapist" directory of clinicians who run therapy groups across the US, including men's-only groups. The right meta-entry for a man seeking clinician-led group therapy — the locator surfaces practitioners by state and specialty.

entries.name: AMVETS (American Veterans)
entries.description: Veterans service organization founded in 1944, congressionally chartered, open to all US military veterans of any era including currently serving members of the Reserves and National Guard. Operates roughly 1,400 posts across the US providing fellowship, benefits advocacy, and community service. Distinguishes from [[Veterans of Foreign Wars]] (foreign-service requirement) and [[The American Legion]] (broader but excludes Reserves) by including currently-serving Reservists.

entries.name: ANAVETS (Army, Navy & Air Force Veterans in Canada)
entries.description: The oldest Canadian veterans organization, founded in 1840 (originally as the Army & Navy Veterans Association). Operates units across Canada providing fellowship, advocacy, and community service. Smaller in absolute size than the [[Royal Canadian Legion]] but with deeper historical continuity — pre-Confederation roots.

entries.name: Ancient Order of Hibernians (AOH)
entries.description: Irish-American Catholic fraternal society founded in 1836 in New York City. Open exclusively to Catholic men of Irish ancestry; local "divisions" across the US run charitable work, Irish cultural preservation, and St. Patrick's Day parade organization. Strongest concentration in the Northeast (NY, NJ, MA, PA, CT) and major Catholic cities (Chicago, Cleveland, San Francisco). The Ladies Ancient Order of Hibernians (LAOH) is a parallel women's organization.

entries.name: Andy's Man Club
entries.description: UK men's peer-support and suicide-prevention community founded in 2016 by Luke Ambler in memory of his brother-in-law Andy Roberts. Operates approximately 200 weekly Monday-night peer-support groups across the UK. Free, anonymous, peer-led. The motto is "It's OK to talk." Has become one of the most-recognized UK men's-mental-health movements.

entries.name: Anglican Church of Canada Men's Ministries
entries.description: Men's ministry network of the Anglican Church of Canada — the Canadian member province of the Anglican Communion. Local men's groups at member parishes run study, retreats, and service. The Brotherhood of St. Andrew has Canadian chapters operating in coordination with the broader US/global Brotherhood structure (see [[Brotherhood of St Andrew]]).
entries._filename: Anglican Church of Canada Mens Ministries.md

entries.name: Anglican Men's Fellowship — Diocese of Jamaica & The Cayman Islands
entries.description: Men's-fellowship network of the Anglican Diocese of Jamaica & The Cayman Islands, the Jamaican-and-Cayman component of the Church in the Province of the West Indies. Operates parish-level fellowship structures across Jamaican Anglican parishes (~150+) plus Cayman Islands. Activities include monthly fellowship meetings, parish service, and diocesan men's events. The Anglican Church has deep historical roots in Jamaica (since 1655) as the established colonial church; substantial absolute Anglican population.

entries.name: Anglican Men's Fellowship — Anglican Church of Kenya (ACK)
entries.description: Men's-fellowship network of the Anglican Church of Kenya (ACK), one of the larger Anglican provinces in Africa. Operates parish-level, diocesan, and provincial structures across the ACK's ~30+ dioceses. Activities include monthly fellowship meetings, evangelical mission, pastoral care, and provincial men's conferences.

entries.name: Anglican Men's Society of the Church of Nigeria
entries.description: Men's-fellowship network of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion) — the largest Anglican province globally by active membership. Operates parish-level, diocesan, and provincial structures across the Church of Nigeria's ~160+ dioceses. Activities include monthly fellowship meetings, evangelical mission, pastoral care, and the annual provincial men's conference.

entries.name: Anglican Sheng Kung Hui (Hong Kong) Men's Fellowship
entries.description: Men's-fellowship network of Hong Kong Sheng Kung Hui (HKSKH), the autonomous Anglican Province covering Hong Kong and Macau (separated from the Anglican Church in China after 1949 and made an independent Province in 1998). Operates parish-level fellowship structures across HKSKH's Hong Kong Island, Eastern Kowloon, and Western Kowloon dioceses, in both English and Cantonese. St John's Cathedral (Central, since 1849) is the historic flagship and host of the most-prominent English-medium men's gatherings.
entries._filename: Anglican Sheng Kung Hui Mens Fellowship.md

entries.name: Australian Men's Health Forum (AMHF)
entries.description: National peak body for men's health in Australia. Operates as a research, advocacy, and convening organisation linking the men's-health, men's-mental-health, and men's-services sectors. Publishes the long-running *AMHF News* newsletter, hosts the National Men's Health Gathering, and maintains a directory of Australian men's-health and men's-services organisations that complements (and overlaps with) this directory.

entries.name: Australian Men's Shed Association
entries.description: National peak body for the roughly 1,200 local Men's Sheds across Australia — community workshops where men gather to make and build things, plus share tea, conversation, and informal support. Australia is the **origin** of the global Men's Sheds movement (regional Victoria, late 1990s), and AMSA was formalised as the national association in 2007. Sheds are typically free or low-cost, operate weekly, and are particularly meaningful for older men in retirement, isolation, or post-bereavement.

entries.name: Authentic Manhood / Men's Fraternity
entries.description: Christian men's ministry curriculum and movement founded by Pastor Robert Lewis, originally as "Men's Fraternity" at Fellowship Bible Church in Little Rock in 1990. Programs use video-based curriculum (notably "33 The Series") supported by small-group discussion, attempting to systematically address what Lewis calls the "four pillars of authentic manhood." Active in churches across the US through curriculum adoption.

entries.name: Backcountry Hunters & Anglers Canada
entries.description: Canadian chapter of [[Backcountry Hunters and Anglers]], founded 2017. Public-land conservation paired with active hunting/fishing culture. Operates provincial chapters in BC, Alberta, Ontario, and other provinces. Mixed-gender by design; men's-gathering function emerges through chapter events, "Pint Nights," and habitat-stewardship days similar to the US BHA.

entries.name: Backcountry Hunters & Anglers
entries.description: Hunting, fishing, and public-land conservation organization, founded in 2004 in Oregon. Operates state and regional chapters across the US — chapter meetings, "Pint Nights," habitat-stewardship days, and educational events constitute the recurring gathering. Officially mixed-gender; in practice many chapter events function as significant men's-gathering sites in regions where hunting and fishing remain male-coded activities.

entries.name: Bahá'í Faith (US Community)
entries.description: Independent monotheistic religion with US community since 1894 and approximately 150,000 US members. The US National Spiritual Assembly is headquartered near the Bahá'í House of Worship in Wilmette, IL. Local Bahá'í communities ("Local Spiritual Assemblies") gather for the Nineteen Day Feasts (held every 19 days), study circles, devotional gatherings, and youth-development programs.

entries.name: BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha
entries.description: Global Swaminarayan Hindu denomination with one of the largest US temple networks, including the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham Mahamandir in Robbinsville, NJ — the largest Hindu temple in the US (opened 2023). Local BAPS centers (mandirs) across the US run age-graded men's groups including Bal Mandals (boys), Yuvak Mandals (young men), and Karyakar networks (adult male volunteers and seva). Strong men's-specific structure within a fundamentally family-oriented religious community.

entries.name: Bellwood Health Services
entries.description: Toronto-based addiction-treatment centre with residential and outpatient programs. Part of the Edgewood Health Network alongside [[Edgewood Treatment Centre]] in BC. Mixed-gender residential with separate men's-track programming and specialized programs for first responders, veterans, and professionals. Insurance-funded for many; private-pay also.

entries.name: Beyond Blue
entries.description: Australia's largest mental-health charity, founded in 2000 by former Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett. Operates a 24/7 phone and webchat support service (1300 22 4636), peer-moderated online forums, and substantial men's-specific mental-health programs and resources. Not men-only, but its men's-mental-health programming and the heavily-male user base of its forums make it a primary entry point for Australian men in distress.

entries.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Canada
entries.description: Canadian counterpart to [[Big Brothers Big Sisters of America]], operating as a separate Canadian organization since 1916 (Toronto). Operates roughly 100 local agencies across Canada. The "Big Brother" program matches adult male volunteers with boys for one-to-one mentoring relationships of at least one year. Free for participants; volunteer Bigs go through screening and training.

entries.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters of America
entries.description: National youth-mentorship organization founded in 1904, operating roughly 230 local affiliated agencies across the US. The "Big Brother" program matches adult male volunteers ("Bigs") with boys ("Littles") for one-to-one mentoring relationships of at least one year's duration. Free for participants; volunteer Bigs go through screening, background checks, and training. Listed under `rites` because the boy-meets-mentor relationship is the program's core, and the adult Big-volunteer cohort constitutes a meaningful men's-mentorship community.
entries._filename: Big Brothers Big Sisters of America.md

entries.name: Big Buddy Mentoring
entries.description: New Zealand mentoring charity that matches fatherless boys with screened, trained adult-male mentors for ongoing one-to-one relationship over years. Founded in 1997. Operates primarily in the upper North Island (Auckland, Waikato, Bay of Plenty), with nation-wide aspirations. Vetted intake — mentors undergo full screening and training before being matched. Free for the boy and his family.

entries.name: Black Fathers Foundation
entries.description: Non-profit organization focused on supporting Black fathers through programming, advocacy, mentorship, and community-building. Operates in cities across the US through chapters or program partnerships. Listed alongside [[Concerned Black Men National]] and [[100 Black Men of America]] for Black men's gathering coverage — Black Fathers Foundation focuses specifically on fatherhood while CBM and 100 Black Men have broader civic mentorship missions.

entries.name: Light of Jesus Family — Brotherhood
entries.description: Men's-fellowship network of Light of Jesus Family (LOJ), a Filipino Catholic charismatic lay community founded 1980 by Bo Sanchez. LOJ operates the long-running Kerygma Community / Feast worship gatherings (often >50,000 attendance per major gathering) plus the smaller-scale Brotherhood / men's-cohort tracks. Free participation; Catholic-charismatic frame with Bo Sanchez's distinctive popular-spirituality and prosperity-adjacent teachings.
entries._filename: Bo Sanchez Light of Jesus Brotherhood.md

entries.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of America
entries.description: National network of after-school clubs for youth ages 6–18, with origins in 1860 (Hartford, CT) and the modern federation founded in 1956. Operates roughly 5,000 club sites across the US, plus military bases and Native American lands. Co-ed since the 1990 merger of Boys' Clubs of America and the Girls Clubs; adult male volunteers and staff constitute significant mentorship presence. Listed under `rites` for its youth-development mission and the men's-mentorship structure within the broader program.
entries._filename: Boys and Girls Clubs of America.md

entries.name: The Boys' Brigade in Malaysia
entries.description: Malaysia's national Boys' Brigade organisation, founded 1946 (the first BB Company in Singapore-Malaya territory was actually established 1930 in Singapore; Malaysia's separate national body emerged after independence). School-based weekly companies for boys aged 9–18 in Christian-rooted character, leadership, and faith development. Active across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak; particularly strong in mission-school networks and Methodist / Anglican / Catholic-affiliated schools.

entries.name: The Boys' Brigade in Singapore
entries.description: Singapore's national Boys' Brigade organisation, founded 1930 and one of the oldest BB national bodies outside the UK. School-based weekly companies for boys aged 9–18 in Christian-rooted character, leadership, and faith development. ~5,000 active members across most major Singapore secondary schools. Uniformed-youth structure with parade nights, badges, camps, and the long-running Sharity Gift Box charity drive. Christian frame throughout but inclusive of non-Christian boys at participating schools.

entries.name: The Boys' Brigade
entries.description: Christian uniformed youth organization for boys ages 5–18, founded in 1883 in Glasgow by William Alexander Smith — predates Boy Scouts (1907) and is the original modern Christian boys' organization. Combines drill, education, badges, and Christian formation. Active in the UK, Republic of Ireland, Northern Ireland, and former British Commonwealth countries; smaller US presence as Christian Service Brigade adopted some Boys' Brigade structures.

entries.name: Boys to Men Mentoring Network
entries.description: Mentorship and rites-of-passage program for adolescent boys, founded in San Diego in 1996. Combines weekly mentor-led groups for boys with multi-day "Adventure" weekends led by adult male volunteers. Adult mentors are vetted and trained. US chapter network is concentrated in California with expansions across the country and abroad.

entries.name: Benevolent and Protective Order of Elks (BPOE)
entries.description: US-only fraternal order founded in 1868 in New York City, operating roughly 2,000 lodges across all 50 states. Lodges meet weekly for fellowship, charitable work, and signature programs including extensive veterans support, scholarships, and youth programs. Membership requires belief in God, US citizenship, and 21+. Co-ed since 1995, but lodges remain male-majority in many cities.

entries.name: Brotherhood of Saint Andrew Canada
entries.description: Canadian chapters of the Brotherhood of St. Andrew, the international Anglican men's organization founded in 1883 (see US [[Brotherhood of St Andrew]] entry). Canadian chapters operate at member parishes within the [[Anglican Church of Canada Mens Ministries]] tradition. Members commit to weekly disciplines of prayer, study, and service.

entries.name: Brotherhood of St Andrew India
entries.description: Anglican / Mar Thoma men's-fellowship presence in India, operating through the Church of North India (CNI), Church of South India (CSI), and the Mar Thoma Syrian Church. The Brotherhood of St Andrew was founded 1883 in the United States; Indian chapters exist particularly in Kerala (Mar Thoma heartland), Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Activities include monthly fellowship, parish service, and the Brotherhood's "Rule of Prayer and Service" — a daily commitment to prayer for the spread of Christ's kingdom among men.

entries.name: Brotherhood of St. Andrew
entries.description: Men's ministry of the Episcopal Church (and select Anglican parishes), founded in Chicago in 1883 — the oldest continuously-operating Episcopal men's organization in the US. Chapters at member parishes commit to weekly disciplines of prayer, study, and service. Active in Episcopal cathedrals and parishes across the US, with international counterparts elsewhere in the Anglican Communion.

entries.name: Brothers in Arms NZ
entries.description: NZ men's peer-support charity running free local group meetings designed as low-barrier entry points for men experiencing mental-health distress, isolation, or grief. Modeled in spirit on UK [[Andys Man Club]] — peer-led, weekly, free, anonymous, "it's OK to talk." Operates across multiple NZ regions with growing reach.

entries.name: Buddhist Churches of America (BCA)
entries.description: Mainstream Buddhist denomination in the US for Jodo Shinshu (True Pure Land) Buddhism, founded in 1899 as the Buddhist Mission of North America. Approximately 60 temples across the US, concentrated in California and Hawaii where Japanese-American Buddhist communities historically settled. Each temple has a sangha (community) with men's-specific groups (Buddhist Brotherhood / Sangha) running parallel to women's and youth divisions. Free, donation-supported.

entries.name: CALM (Campaign Against Living Miserably)
entries.description: UK men's-suicide-prevention charity founded in 2006. Operates the CALM helpline (5pm to midnight, free), webchat support, and a community/awareness platform. Suicide is the leading killer of men under 50 in the UK; CALM's mission centers on changing that. Not a gathering itself but a critical crisis-support layer alongside [[Andys Man Club]] and [[Samaritans]] in the UK men's-mental-health-crisis landscape.

entries.name: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH)
entries.description: Canada's largest mental-health and addiction teaching hospital, located in Toronto. Founded in 1998 through merger of four predecessor institutions. Operates inpatient, outpatient, and community programs including some men's-specific services for substance use, concurrent disorders, and trauma. Public-funded through Ontario healthcare; many programs are free or covered.

entries.name: Canadian Baptist Ministries
entries.description: Umbrella body for the four main Canadian Baptist Convention bodies — the Canadian Baptists of Atlantic Canada, the Canadian Baptists of Ontario and Quebec, the Canadian Baptists of Western Canada, and the Union d'Églises Baptistes Francophones du Canada (French-language). Men's ministries operate at convention and congregation levels with study, retreats, and service projects. Theological orientation generally mainline-evangelical.

entries.name: Canadian Cadet Programs (Sea / Army / Air Cadets)
entries.description: Canadian Forces–sponsored youth program for ages 12–18, comprising the Royal Canadian Sea Cadets, Royal Canadian Army Cadets, and Royal Canadian Air Cadets. Free for cadets — uniforms, training, and summer-camp programs are funded by the Canadian government. Adult mentors include serving and former Canadian Armed Forces members plus civilian volunteers (the Civilian Instructor Cadre).

entries.name: Canadian Centre for Men and Families (CCMF)
entries.description: Multi-city Canadian organization providing peer support, mental-health services, and family support to men, founded in 2014 with locations in Toronto, Calgary, Ottawa, Halifax, and other cities. Programs include peer-led support groups, fatherhood programs, men's mental-health counseling, and crisis support. Free or low-cost for participants.
entries._filename: Canadian Centre for Men and Families.md

entries.name: Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA)
entries.description: Largest Canadian mental health charity, founded in 1918, with branches across all provinces and one territory. Many CMHA branches run men's-specific peer-support groups, mental-wellness workshops, and crisis-line services. Programs vary by branch and province; the national umbrella supports advocacy and research while local branches deliver direct services.

entries.name: Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines (CBCP) Men's Ministry
entries.description: Men's-ministry coordination of the Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines, operating through ~86 territorial dioceses and ~10 military / personal apostolic structures. Parish-level men's groups follow varied forms — Holy Name Society confraternities, Knights of Columbus councils, Cursillo de Cristiandad alumni groups, and lay-renewal-movement chapters (CFC BCBP, El Shaddai, Light of Jesus). The CBCP itself coordinates national pastoral programmes; per-parish men's-fellowship contacts vary widely.
entries._filename: Catholic Bishops Conference Philippines Mens Ministry.md

entries.name: Catholic Diocese of Hong Kong Men's Ministry
entries.description: Men's-ministry network of the Catholic Diocese of Hong Kong (founded 1841 as Apostolic Prefecture; Diocese since 1946), one of the larger Catholic dioceses in East Asia. Operates parish-level men's-fellowship structures across Hong Kong's ~50+ Catholic parishes — including [[Holy Name Society]]-style confraternities. Substantial Filipino-Catholic men's gatherings concentrate around parishes serving the Filipino domestic-worker community (St Joseph's Garden Road, Wan Chai; The Holy Spirit, etc.). Bilingual operation in English, Cantonese, and Filipino.
entries._filename: Catholic Diocese of Hong Kong Mens Ministry.md

entries.name: Catholic Men Association of Kenya
entries.description: Lay men's body of the Kenya Conference of Catholic Bishops (KCCB) — the men's parallel to the Catholic Women Association (CWA). Operates parish-level, diocesan, and national structures across all Kenyan Catholic dioceses. Membership requires being a practising Catholic man; activities include monthly meetings, parish service, retreats, and the annual association assembly.

entries.name: Catholic Men Organisation of Nigeria (CMON)
entries.description: Official lay men's body of the Catholic Bishops' Conference of Nigeria — the men's parallel to the Catholic Women Organisation (CWO). Operates parish-level, diocesan, and national structures across all Nigerian Catholic dioceses (~50+ dioceses). Membership requires being a practising Catholic man; activities include monthly meetings, parish service, retreats, and the annual CMON National Conference. Significantly larger in absolute scale than most Western-Catholic men's fraternal orders given Nigeria's Catholic population.

entries.name: Catholic Men's Society of Ghana
entries.description: Lay men's body associated with the Ghana Catholic Bishops' Conference. Operates parish-level, diocesan, and national structures across Ghanaian Catholic dioceses. Membership requires being a practising Catholic man; activities include monthly meetings, parish service, retreats, and an annual society conference. Counterpart institutional pattern to Catholic men's lay bodies in other African Catholic countries.

entries.name: Catholic War Veterans of the USA
entries.description: Congressionally chartered veterans service organization for Catholic men and women who served in US military combat or war-zone deployments, founded in 1935. Operates posts across the US providing fellowship, advocacy, and Catholic-faith-rooted veteran community. Smaller in absolute size than [[Veterans of Foreign Wars]] or [[The American Legion]] but distinctive in its explicit Catholic identity — combines the veteran-fraternal model with parish-level Catholic men's-ministry character.

entries.name: Celebrate Recovery
entries.description: Christian 12-step-influenced recovery program hosted by churches across the US, addressing addictions and what they call "hurts, habits, and hang-ups." Most meetings include open share groups segmented by gender. Free, weekly, and low-friction — a viable door for a man in crisis who's open to a Christian frame.

entries.name: Center for Employment Opportunities (CEO)
entries.description: Reentry employment program founded in 1996 in New York City, now operating in multiple US states. Provides immediate-paid transitional work (typically 4-day-a-week crew labor) plus job-readiness services and full-time job placement for men recently released from incarceration. Free for participants. Independently validated through randomized controlled trials showing significant reductions in recidivism.

entries.name: Centre for Fathering Singapore
entries.description: Singapore charity founded in 2000 to promote active and engaged fatherhood; in 2009 launched the national **Dads for Life** movement in partnership with the Singapore government. Programmes include the Dads for Life Family Life Champions network, fatherhood courses, school-based engagement (e.g. ICAN — Involved-Caring-Available-Networking), and corporate partnerships. Free for participants; widely-recognised national fatherhood programme studied as a model internationally.

entries.name: CFC Brotherhood of Christian Businessmen and Professionals (BCBP)
entries.description: Men's-fellowship arm of Couples for Christ (CFC), the global Filipino-rooted Catholic charismatic lay renewal movement (founded 1981 in Manila; now operating in 165+ countries). The BCBP runs men-specific weekly chapter meetings, retreats, and the Christian Life Program (CLP) — a multi-week introductory teaching series that all CFC members complete. Free participation; Catholic-charismatic frame throughout. Branches operate across the Philippines and in major Filipino-diaspora communities (US, Canada, UK, Australia, Hong Kong, UAE, Saudi Arabia, etc.).
entries._filename: CFC Brotherhood of Christian Businessmen and Professionals.md

entries.name: CFK Africa (Carolina for Kibera)
entries.description: Kenyan-led NGO operating in Kibera (Africa's largest urban informal settlement) and other Nairobi communities, founded in 2001 as a partnership between Kenyan community leaders and the University of North Carolina. Programmes include the Taka Ni Pato youth-environmental movement, sports-for-development (the long-running Kibera Soccer League), girls' empowerment, healthcare, and the Daraja Boys' programme — a youth-mentoring intervention for adolescent boys at risk of gang involvement.

entries.name: Chabad-Lubavitch (Local Centers)
entries.description: International Hasidic Jewish outreach movement with thousands of Chabad Houses and centers across the US. Each center is independent and run by a Chabad rabbi-couple, but most host daily morning minyan (men's prayer), men's Torah study, and other men-specific gatherings as part of broader community programming. Listed as a meta-entry pointing to chabad.org's center locator; intake is welcoming to Jewish men of any background, including unaffiliated and beginner-level.

entries.name: Christian Motorcyclists Association UK
entries.description: UK Christian motorcyclist ministry, the British counterpart to the US [[Christian Motorcyclists Association]]. Members ride together for fellowship and street-level evangelism at biker events and rallies across the UK. Various UK Christian biker ministries exist; CMA UK is one of the more-established, with a presence at major UK rallies (BMF Show, etc.).

entries.name: Christian Motorcyclists Association (CMA)
entries.description: Christian motorcyclist ministry founded in 1975 in Hatfield, AR. Local chapters across the US gather for rides, charitable work, and street-level evangelism. Distinctive in combining motorcycle culture with explicit Christian formation. Not all CMA members ride; "Friends of CMA" supports the ministry without riding. Men's-gathering function emerges through chapter rides, work events, and the National Rally.

entries.name: Christian Reformed Church Men's Ministry
entries.description: Men's ministry of the Christian Reformed Church in North America (CRCNA), a Dutch Reformed (Calvinist) denomination with US members concentrated in Michigan (especially Grand Rapids), Iowa, Illinois, California, and Washington. Local men's groups at member congregations run study, retreats, and service projects within an explicit Reformed-Calvinist theological frame.

entries.name: Christian Service Brigade (CSB)
entries.description: Cross-denominational evangelical Christian boys' program founded in 1937, with active US and Canadian operations. Boys ages 7–17 join age-graded sections (Stockade for younger boys, Battalion for older boys) led by adult men trained as CSB leaders. Programs combine Christian formation, outdoor skills, and badge-based advancement.

entries.name: Christian Surfers United States
entries.description: US chapter of Christian Surfers International, a global Christian surfing ministry founded in Australia in 1977. US presence centers on coastal communities (CA, FL, HI, the Carolinas, Oregon). Local chapters host beach gatherings, paddle-outs, and Christian formation rooted in surfing culture. Mixed-gender but male-majority given surf demographics.

entries.name: Christian Vision for Men (CVM)
entries.description: UK evangelical men's ministry founded in 1996 by Carl Beech. Hosts annual men's conferences (notably "The Gathering"), publishes resources, and supports local church-based men's groups across the UK. Theologically evangelical Protestant.

entries.name: City Dads Group
entries.description: Network of dad meetup groups in major US cities, founded in NYC in 2008. Local chapters host playdates, dad's nights out, and discussion groups; entry is free and informal. Best for new and active dads looking for peer connection in an urban environment.

entries.name: Civil Air Patrol (CAP)
entries.description: Congressionally chartered nonprofit and official auxiliary of the US Air Force, founded in 1941. Three core missions: emergency services (search and rescue, disaster response), aerospace education, and a cadet program for youth ages 12–21. Adult members serve as senior members supporting the cadet program and operations. The cadet program is a meaningful rites-of-passage structure for boys with adult-male mentor presence.

entries.name: Christian Methodist Episcopal (CME) Men
entries.description: Men's ministry of the Christian Methodist Episcopal Church (CME), one of the three historic Black Methodist denominations alongside [[AME Sons of Allen]] and [[AME Zion Men]]. Founded in 1870 in Jackson, TN as the Colored Methodist Episcopal Church (renamed in 1954). Local men's groups at member CME congregations across the US.

entries.name: Cocaine Anonymous
entries.description: 12-step fellowship for recovery from cocaine and other mind-altering substances, founded in 1982. The fellowship's tradition is open to anyone with "a desire to stop using cocaine and all other mind-altering substances," making it cross-addiction friendly. Phone, online, and in-person meetings nationally; free, anonymous, peer-led.

entries.name: Codependents Anonymous (CoDA)
entries.description: 12-step fellowship for recovery from codependency patterns in relationships, founded in 1986 in Phoenix, AZ. Meetings address compulsive caretaking, people-pleasing, controlling behaviors, and difficulty maintaining functional intimate relationships. In-person and online meetings nationwide. Free, anonymous, peer-led.

entries.name: COGIC Department of Men
entries.description: Men's department of the Church of God in Christ (COGIC), the largest Pentecostal denomination of African Americans, founded in 1907 by Bishop Charles Harrison Mason. Headquartered in Memphis, TN. Department of Men programs operate at the local-church, district, jurisdiction, and national levels with annual gatherings drawing thousands of men. The COGIC Holy Convocation in Memphis (held in November) is among the largest Black Christian gatherings in the US.

entries.name: Combat Stress
entries.description: UK military mental-health charity founded in 1919 (originally the Ex-Servicemen's Welfare Society), among the oldest veteran mental-health organizations in the world. Provides clinical mental-health services, peer support, and a 24/7 helpline for UK veterans dealing with PTSD, depression, moral injury, and combat trauma. Free for UK veterans.

entries.name: Compassion Prison Project
entries.description: Trauma-informed prison program founded in 2018 by Fritzi Horstman, focused on healing childhood trauma (Adverse Childhood Experiences / ACEs) inside US correctional facilities. Programs combine ACE-survey conversations, circle work, and trauma education with men inside, and training outside volunteers to facilitate. Free for participants; volunteer-driven on the outside.

entries.name: Concerned Black Men National (CBM)
entries.description: National non-profit founded in Philadelphia in 1975, focused on Black male mentorship, fatherhood support, and youth development. Local chapters across the US run mentor programs for boys, fatherhood programs for adult men, and community service. CBM operates the "CARES Mentoring Movement" and other ongoing programs alongside chapter-based work.

entries.name: Conquer Series
entries.description: Ten-week video-curriculum series for Christian men's sexual integrity, produced by Kingdom Works Productions and led by Jeremy Wiles. Used by churches and small groups across the US — typically watched together with weekly small-group accountability discussion. Cinematic production quality differentiates it from earlier workbook-based ministries. Christian frame is explicit; cessation of pornography use is the core goal.

entries.name: Christian Reformed Church Canada
entries.description: Canadian member region of the [[Christian Reformed Church Mens Ministry]] (CRC of North America). Dutch Reformed (Calvinist) denomination with approximately 40,000 Canadian members concentrated in Ontario, BC, and Alberta, where Dutch immigrant communities settled post-WWII. Local men's groups at member CRC congregations within the CRCNA's bi-national structure.

entries.name: Crystal Meth Anonymous (CMA)
entries.description: 12-step fellowship for recovery from methamphetamine and crystal-meth dependence, founded in 1994 in West Hollywood, CA. In-person and online meetings are free, anonymous, peer-led. Particularly active in cities with significant gay-male populations where meth use has been a persistent issue, plus the Mountain West and rural areas with documented meth problems.

entries.name: Cursillo Movement Canada (Mouvement des Cursillos du Canada)
entries.description: Canadian member of the global Cursillo Movement — Catholic three-day retreat program (see US [[Cursillo Movement]] entry). Particularly active in Quebec where the Mouvement des Cursillos opérates in French; English-language Cursillos run in Ontario, the Atlantic provinces, and other dioceses. Group Reunions and Ultreyas continue post-weekend, providing ongoing Catholic men's community.

entries.name: Cursillos de Cristiandad (Cursillo Movement)
entries.description: Catholic three-day retreat movement that began in Spain in 1944 (the name means "short course") and arrived in the US in 1957. Cursillo weekends are gender-segregated — men's weekends and women's weekends run separately — combining teaching, sharing, and small-group reflection. After the weekend, participants join "Group Reunions" (small ongoing accountability groups) and periodic regional gatherings called "Ultreyas." Active in most US Catholic dioceses with both English and Spanish tracks; Spanish-language Cursillos are particularly significant in dioceses with large Hispanic populations.

entries.name: Dad 2.0 Summit
entries.description: Annual conference and ongoing community for fathers, founded 2012, oriented toward modern fatherhood and dad bloggers / content creators. The annual summit (typically held in February or March in a different US city each year) includes panels, workshops, and structured networking. An active online community continues year-round through a private Facebook group and similar channels. Conference attendance is fee-based; community participation is free.

entries.name: Dads Group Australia
entries.description: Australian fatherhood charity supporting a national network of free local Dads Groups — peer-led gatherings of new and existing fathers with their kids, modeled loosely on traditional mothers' groups but designed for dads. Founded in 2014. Groups typically meet weekly or fortnightly at parks, cafes, libraries, or community centres. Free to join; volunteer-run with light national infrastructure for support and training.

entries.name: Defy Ventures
entries.description: Entrepreneurship and personal-development program for currently and formerly incarcerated men, founded 2010. Combines in-prison curriculum with post-release coaching and volunteer mentorship from outside business professionals. Free for participants; supported by volunteer engagement and donor funding.

entries.name: DeMolay International
entries.description: International fraternal youth organization for young men ages 12–21, founded in 1919 in Kansas City, MO. Sponsored by Freemasonry but does not require Masonic affiliation for membership. Local chapters operate across the US with adult Masonic advisors providing mentorship structure. Programs combine ritual ceremony, civic service, and leadership development.

entries.name: Disabled American Veterans (DAV)
entries.description: Congressionally chartered veterans service organization founded in 1920 for veterans wounded or disabled in service. Operates roughly 1,300 chapters across the US, plus a national network of service officers who help veterans navigate VA disability claims and benefits. Chapter meetings provide brotherhood and mentorship; the service-officer work is among the most-used veterans-benefits navigation resources in the country.

entries.name: Disciples of Christ Men's Ministry
entries.description: Men's ministry of the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ), a mainline Protestant denomination rooted in the early-19th-century Restoration Movement. Local chapters at member congregations run study groups, service projects, and an annual gathering. Smaller in absolute size than [[United Methodist Men]] or the Presbyterian/Lutheran men's ministries but distinctive within the Restoration Movement tradition.

entries.name: Ducks Unlimited Canada
entries.description: Canadian waterfowl and wetlands conservation nonprofit founded in 1938, the Canadian parallel to [[Ducks Unlimited]] (US DU). Conducts wetlands habitat work across Canada with chapter networks running banquets, field events, and youth mentor programs. Men's-gathering function emerges through chapter culture similar to US DU, especially in Prairies provinces, Atlantic Canada, and Ontario.

entries.name: Ducks Unlimited (DU)
entries.description: Waterfowl-conservation nonprofit founded in 1937, with approximately 700,000 members and chapter-banquet networks across the US. Mission centers on wetland and waterfowl-habitat conservation, but the chapter banquets, sportsmen's nights, and youth-mentor programs function as significant men's-gathering sites in regions with substantial duck-hunting culture.

entries.name: Eastern Orthodox Parish Men's Groups
entries.description: Eastern Orthodox parishes across the US — operating under multiple jurisdictions including OCA (Orthodox Church in America), Greek Orthodox Archdiocese, Antiochian Orthodox, ROCOR (Russian Orthodox Outside Russia), Serbian Orthodox, Romanian Orthodox, Bulgarian Orthodox, Coptic Orthodox, Ethiopian Orthodox, and others — typically maintain parish men's groups with variable programming. Most gather monthly for fellowship, charity, study, and discussion. The Assembly of Canonical Orthodox Bishops serves as a coordinating umbrella and parish-finder.

entries.name: Eastern Orthodox Parishes Canada
entries.description: Eastern Orthodox parishes across Canada — operating under multiple jurisdictions including OCA Canada, Antiochian Orthodox Archdiocese of Canada, Greek Orthodox Metropolis of Toronto (Canada), Russian Orthodox Canadian dioceses (ROCOR and Moscow Patriarchate), Serbian Orthodox, Ukrainian Orthodox Church of Canada, Romanian Orthodox, Coptic Orthodox, and others. Most parishes maintain men's groups with variable programming.

entries.name: Easton Mountain
entries.description: Retreat centre and intentional community for gay, bisexual, queer, and questioning men, located on 175 acres in Greenwich, NY (upstate). Founded 2001. Hosts dozens of weekend and week-long retreats annually — including the long-running Body Electric workshops, naked yoga and meditation retreats, contemplative-Christian gay men's retreats, sober-recovery weekends, and creative arts intensives. Interfaith and inclusive of secular participants. Fee-based with sliding-scale options on selected programmes.

entries.name: Edgewood Treatment Centre
entries.description: Major Canadian residential addiction-treatment centre in Nanaimo, BC, founded in 1994 — flagship facility of the Edgewood Health Network. 12-step rooted, abstinence-based, with mixed-gender residential programs plus separate men's-track programming. Insurance-funded for many participants; private-pay also.

entries.name: Evangelical Lutheran Church in Canada (ELCIC) Men
entries.description: Men's network of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Canada (ELCIC), the largest mainline Lutheran denomination in Canada. Canadian counterpart to the US-based [[Lutheran Men in Mission]] (ELCA). Local men's groups at member ELCIC congregations run study, retreats, and service projects.

entries.name: Esalen Institute
entries.description: Big Sur, CA retreat center founded in 1962, considered the birthplace of the human-potential movement. Hosts hundreds of week-long and weekend workshops year-round on topics including emotional integration, somatic work, gestalt therapy, and personal-growth practice. Mixed-gender by default, with periodic men's-only retreats and workshops. Costs are significant but include lodging at the Big Sur property.

entries.name: Evryman
entries.description: National community of men's groups built around emotional fluency, vulnerability, and peer support. Runs weekly virtual and in-person groups, multi-day retreats, and an online member community. Free intro events lead into paid ongoing groups; intake is straightforward.

entries.name: F3 Canada
entries.description: Canadian chapters and AOs (areas of operation) of [[F3 Nation]] — the free, peer-led men's outdoor workout brotherhood. Active in Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary, Ottawa, and other Canadian cities. Same format as US F3: dawn workouts, peer-led, free, three Fs (Fitness, Fellowship, Faith). The third F is framed broadly enough to include any belief in something larger than self; Canadian secular culture often interprets it lightly.

entries.name: F3 Nation
entries.description: National network of free, peer-led men's outdoor workouts held before dawn — five days a week in most cities. Founded 2011 in Charlotte, NC; now operates thousands of "AOs" (areas of operation) across all 50 states. The three Fs are Fitness, Fellowship, and Faith — the third is framed broadly enough to include any belief in something larger than self, and the workouts themselves carry no overt religious content.

entries.name: Faithful & True Ministries
entries.description: Christian sexual integrity ministry founded by Dr. Mark Laaser (1950–2019), based in Eden Prairie, MN. Programs include intensive workshops for men and couples dealing with sexual addiction and intimacy disorders, plus small-group materials for use in churches. Mark Laaser's *Healing the Wounds of Sexual Addiction* was a foundational text in the Christian sexual-integrity space.

entries.name: Father a Nation
entries.description: South African Christian men's-discipleship and fatherhood organisation running QUEST — a multi-week men's group process focused on identity, fatherhood, and healing father-wounds — through churches, communities, and prisons across South Africa. Founded 2010. Free participation; QUEST is delivered in church, community, and correctional-facility settings nationwide. Christian framing throughout.

entries.name: Father & Child Trust
entries.description: NZ charity supporting fathers and father-figures across the spectrum — new dads, separated dads, dads with young children, dads facing care-and-protection issues. Operates regional offices (Christchurch flagship, plus Auckland and others) running peer support groups, parenting courses, and one-to-one casework. Free or low-cost. Distinctively engages with separated-fathers' family-court experience as part of its scope.

entries.name: Fellowship of Evangelical Baptist Churches in Canada (FEBCC)
entries.description: Conservative evangelical Canadian Baptist body, the second-largest Canadian Baptist denomination after the [[Canadian Baptist Ministries]] mainline-evangelical umbrella. Approximately 500 member churches across Canada. Local men's ministries at member congregations within an explicit conservative-evangelical theological frame — stronger emphasis on biblical authority and traditional doctrine than the broader CBM tradition.

entries.name: Federation of Jewish Men's Clubs
entries.description: Brotherhood organization affiliated with Conservative Jewish synagogues across the US, founded in 1929. Local clubs at member synagogues run social events, men's-focused study, charitable activities, and signature programs like "Hearing Men's Voices" on emotional vulnerability and mental health. The Conservative-movement parallel to [[Men of Reform Judaism]].

entries.name: Friends General Conference Quaker Men
entries.description: Friends General Conference (FGC), the largest unprogrammed-tradition (silent worship) branch of Quakerism in the US. Yearly Meetings under FGC umbrella include Philadelphia, NY, Baltimore, New England, Lake Erie, Northern, Ohio Valley, Southeastern, and others. Men's-specific gathering varies — some yearly meetings have men's working groups, men's-of-color groups, and dedicated men's retreats; the broader pattern is mixed-gender silent worship with informal men's connection.

entries.name: First Nations Health Authority (FNHA, BC)
entries.description: First Nations Health Authority of British Columbia, the first province-wide First Nations-governed health authority in Canada, established in 2013. Delivers health services and wellness programming to First Nations communities across BC. Men's-specific programming runs through community-level partnerships including men's-wellness initiatives at urban Friendship Centres and rural First Nations health stations.

entries.name: Fraternal Order of Eagles (FOE)
entries.description: Fraternal organization founded in 1898 in Seattle, WA, with aeries (local lodges) across the US and Canada. Notable for civic-charitable work including driving the establishment of Mother's Day (1908) and significant medical-research charity (Diabetes, Children's Heart). Now formally co-ed (since 1981); many aeries remain male-majority. Lodge-and-canteen culture similar to [[BPOE Elks]] and [[Loyal Order of Moose]].

entries.name: Freemasonry (US Grand Lodges)
entries.description: Fraternal order operating through state-level Grand Lodges with thousands of local lodges across the US. Lodges meet monthly for ritual, fellowship, and charitable work. Membership requires petitioning a local lodge, vouching by current members, and a unanimous ballot — a slow but real door to a long-running brotherhood. Prince Hall Masonry, with origins in Black American masonic history, operates parallel Grand Lodges in most states and warrants a separate entry.

entries.name: National FFA Organization (Future Farmers of America)
entries.description: National agricultural-education organization for middle and high school students, founded in 1928. Operates through agricultural-education programs in approximately 8,800 US schools with ~700,000 members. Programs combine classroom agricultural education, hands-on Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE) projects, and leadership development through FFA's organizational structure (chapter / state / national levels with annual conventions).

entries.name: Gamblers Anonymous
entries.description: 12-step fellowship for recovery from compulsive gambling, founded in 1957. Meetings happen in most US cities plus online; free, anonymous, peer-led. Same low-barrier structure as [[Alcoholics Anonymous]] applied to gambling — a foundational door for any man in active crisis around gambling losses, sports betting, online wagering, or stock-market compulsion.

entries.name: Gay Spirit Visions
entries.description: Long-running gay-men's spiritual community, founded 1989 in Atlanta, GA. Hosts twice-yearly multi-day spiritual retreats / conferences ("Fall Conference" and "Winter Conference") at The Mountain Retreat Center in Highlands, NC, plus regional men's circles, monthly Atlanta gatherings, and a network of GSV-affiliated chapters. Interfaith and inclusive — Christian, Jewish, Buddhist, Pagan, secular, and other gay men gather for shared spiritual exploration. Fee-based with scholarship options.

entries.name: GMHC (Gay Men's Health Crisis)
entries.description: The world's first and largest HIV/AIDS-services organisation, founded in New York City in January 1982 by Larry Kramer, Paul Popham, Larry Mass, Paul Rapoport, Nathan Fain, and Edmund White — at the very beginning of the AIDS epidemic and decades before the disease had a name. Today GMHC delivers comprehensive HIV-prevention, HIV-positive case management, mental health counselling, substance-use counselling, hot-meal programmes, legal services, and support groups (including ongoing men's groups for HIV-positive long-term survivors, newly-diagnosed men, gay-men in recovery, and others) at its Times Square clinical centre and online. Free for clients.

entries.name: GORUCK
entries.description: Endurance/ruck-march event company and brotherhood, founded in 2008 by former Special Forces operator Jason McCarthy. Hosts overnight endurance events ("Tough," "Heavy," "Selection," "Sandlot") in cities across the US year-round, led by current/former military cadre, that build small-group cohesion through shared physical hardship. The company sells gear, but the durable men's-gathering function is the events plus active local Facebook groups, training meetups, and continuing post-event teams.

entries.name: Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation
entries.description: Major nonprofit addiction-treatment system formed by the 2014 merger of Hazelden Foundation (founded 1949 in Center City, MN) and the Betty Ford Center (founded 1982 in Rancho Mirage, CA). Operates residential and outpatient treatment, sober-living programs, family programs, and Hazelden Publishing. Best known for popularizing the "Minnesota Model" of 12-step-based addiction treatment.

entries.name: The Healing Foundation
entries.description: Australian national Aboriginal- and Torres-Strait-Islander-led organisation focused on intergenerational trauma healing for Stolen Generations survivors and their descendants. Founded 2009 in response to the Australian Government's National Apology (2008). Headquartered in Canberra. Operates the **Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Healing Forum**, the **Men's Healing programme** (which supports Aboriginal men's healing yarning circles and on-country healing camps across Australia), and policy / research / advocacy work. Free participation in member-organisation programming; the Healing Foundation itself is a coordination body funded by Australian government grants and philanthropy.

entries.name: Help for Heroes
entries.description: UK wounded-veterans charity founded in 2007 by Bryn and Emma Parry in response to the Iraq/Afghanistan conflicts. Operates Recovery Centres (Tedworth House, Phoenix House, Plas Y Brenin) plus regional support, sports rehabilitation programs, and family support. Free for UK veterans and their families. Distinguished from older [[Royal British Legion]] (1921 fraternal/welfare) by its specific post-2003 wounded-veterans focus.

entries.name: Heroin Anonymous (HA)
entries.description: 12-step fellowship for recovery from heroin and other opioid addiction, founded in 2004 in Phoenix, AZ. Meetings happen in-person and online, free, anonymous, peer-led. Smaller and newer than [[Alcoholics Anonymous]] but with full 12-step structure adapted for opioid recovery. Has grown significantly with the opioid crisis.

entries.name: Holy Name Society
entries.description: Catholic men's confraternity rooted in devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus, with a presence in many US Catholic parishes. Members typically attend a monthly Mass together, gather afterward for breakfast or fellowship, and run parish service projects. National-level coordination is loose — the National Association of the Holy Name Society (NAHNS) federates participating diocesan unions, but most activity is parish-level. Active most strongly in dioceses with substantial Italian, Irish, and Polish Catholic heritage.

entries.name: Holy Trinity Church Dubai Men's Fellowship
entries.description: Men's-fellowship network of Holy Trinity Church Dubai, the central Anglican / interdenominational Christian church compound in Dubai, founded 1970 (worshipping in the present Jebel Ali / Oud Metha compound since 1983). Holy Trinity hosts more than 100 different congregations across multiple language and denominational expressions (English Anglican, Mar Thoma, Indian Pentecostal, etc.); the men's-fellowship operates primarily through the English-language Anglican congregation with multi-language overflow.
entries._filename: Holy Trinity Church Dubai Mens Fellowship.md

entries.name: Homeboy Industries
entries.description: Los Angeles-based gang-intervention and reentry program founded in 1988 by Father Gregory Boyle, S.J. The program serves formerly-incarcerated and gang-involved men and women through 18-month paid trainee positions in social-enterprise businesses (Homeboy Bakery, Cafe, Silkscreen, etc.), tattoo removal, mental-health services, education, and a deeply embedded culture of "kinship." Free for participants. Largest gang-intervention and rehabilitation program in the US.

entries.name: Hsi Lai Temple / Fo Guang Shan
entries.description: Hsi Lai Temple in Hacienda Heights, CA (opened 1988) is the US flagship of the Taiwan-rooted Fo Guang Shan Mahayana Buddhist order — among the largest Chinese Buddhist temples in the Western hemisphere. The order operates additional US temples in Houston, NYC, Las Vegas, Hawaii, and elsewhere. Men's-specific gathering happens through the Buddha's Light International Association (BLIA) men's chapters and through temple-based study groups, ceremonies, and seva.
entries._filename: Hsi Lai Temple Fo Guang Shan.md

entries.name: I Am A Kind Man / Kizhaay Anishinaabe Niin
entries.description: Indigenous men's program of the Ontario Federation of Indigenous Friendship Centres, focused on engaging Indigenous men in addressing and ending violence against women. Programming includes men's circles, traditional teachings, and community-based workshops grounded in Anishinaabe cultural practice. The Ojibwe phrase "Kizhaay Anishinaabe Niin" means "I am a kind man." Free for participants.

entries.name: Illuman
entries.description: Adult men's rites of passage organization founded in 2010, carrying forward the legacy of Franciscan priest Richard Rohr's "M.A.L.Es" (Men As Learners and Elders) community. Hosts Rohr-influenced rites of passage weekends and ongoing local "Illumination Communities" focused on contemplative spirituality, ego/shadow work, and elder-mentor relationships. Although Rohr's roots are Franciscan Catholic, Illuman is explicitly interfaith and welcomes men of any tradition or none.

entries.name: Inclusive Therapists
entries.description: Find-a-therapist directory focused on culturally-responsive and identity-affirming therapy across the US, with strong representation of BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and neurodivergent clinicians. Listings can be filtered by clinician identity, specialty, modality, and group format. Not men's-specific, but addresses an access gap that [[Psychology Today Therapist Directory]] doesn't always solve well: a man searching for a therapist who shares or understands his cultural context.

entries.name: Independent Order of Odd Fellows (IOOF)
entries.description: Fraternal order founded in Baltimore in 1819 (US branch from the British Manchester Unity), historically the second-largest US fraternal after Freemasonry. Operates lodges across the US — diminished from its 19th-century peak but still active. Symbol is the three-link chain ("Friendship, Love, Truth"). Co-ed since 1971 (Rebekahs, the women's branch, dates to 1851). Membership requires belief in a Supreme Being.

entries.name: Inside Circle
entries.description: California-rooted program running intensive men's-work circles inside US prisons, founded in 1996 by James McLeary. Outside facilitators trained in modern men's-work (mythopoetic, embodied, accountability-focused) lead weekly circles with incarcerated men — most prominently at Folsom State Prison, which was the subject of the 2017 documentary *The Work*. The program runs intentional emotional-development work for men serving long sentences, often for violent offenses, alongside skill-building for the outside men who facilitate.

entries.name: Inside Out Dad
entries.description: Group-based fatherhood curriculum delivered to incarcerated dads inside US correctional facilities. Operated through National Fatherhood Initiative; sessions are facilitated on-site by trained corrections staff or chaplains. Goal is to maintain father-child bond during incarceration and prepare dads for re-entry as engaged fathers.

entries.name: Insight Meditation Society (IMS)
entries.description: Vipassana / Insight Meditation retreat center in Barre, MA, founded in 1975 by Joseph Goldstein, Sharon Salzberg, and Jack Kornfield. The East Coast counterpart to [[Spirit Rock Meditation Center]]. Hosts mixed-gender retreats year-round (silent retreats from weekend to three-month length) including periodic men's-specific weekend retreats. Mostly fee-based with sliding-scale and dana options.

entries.name: Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA)
entries.description: Non-profit veterans organization for post-9/11 era veterans, founded in 2004. Combines advocacy work (notably on the Forever GI Bill and veteran-suicide prevention) with online and in-person community programs. Distinct from older VSOs ([[Veterans of Foreign Wars]], [[The American Legion]], [[AMVETS]]) by its generational focus and digital-first community structure.
entries._filename: Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America.md

entries.name: Iron Sharpens Iron Conferences
entries.description: Network of one-day regional Christian men's conferences across the US, with workshops on marriage, fatherhood, work, and faith. The conferences are the front door — local follow-up depends on the host church. Built for men already inside Protestant Christian orbit; not a low-barrier door for the religiously unaffiliated.

entries.name: ISKCON (Hare Krishna)
entries.description: International Society for Krishna Consciousness, a Vaishnava Hindu movement founded in 1966 in New York City by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada. US temples in major metros (NYC, LA, Chicago, Dallas, Atlanta, Detroit, San Diego, plus farm communities in WV — New Vrindaban — and NC). Men's-specific gathering happens through sankirtan (devotional chanting), kirtan parties, and seva (devotional service) at temples.

entries.name: Islamic Society of North America (ISNA)
entries.description: Largest Muslim umbrella organization in North America, founded in 1981. ISNA's annual convention (typically Labor Day weekend) draws tens of thousands of attendees with extensive men's-specific programming. ISNA's website serves as a meta-locator for affiliated mosques and Islamic centers across the US, where the actual men's gatherings (daily prayer, Friday Jumu'ah, halaqas / study circles) take place.
entries._filename: ISNA Islamic Society of North America.md

entries.name: Junior Chamber International USA (JCI USA)
entries.description: US affiliate of Junior Chamber International, a global service organization for young business leaders ages 18–40. Originally founded in 1915 in St. Louis as the "Junior Citizens" and later "Jaycees." Local chapters across the US run civic projects, leadership-training programs, and networking events. Co-ed since the 1980s.

entries.name: John Howard Society of Canada
entries.description: Federal-provincial network of community-based reentry and criminal-justice-reform organizations in Canada, with the original society founded in 1867 in Toronto. Provincial John Howard Societies operate independently with local programs in residential reentry, employment support, advocacy, and post-release mentorship. Funded primarily through provincial government contracts plus some donor support.

entries.name: Kingdom Men (Tony Evans / Urban Alternative)
entries.description: Christian men's ministry program of Pastor Tony Evans's Urban Alternative platform, based in Dallas. Operates the "Kingdom Man" curriculum — book, sermon series, and small-group materials — for men's discipleship in evangelical churches. Particularly strong reach in Black evangelical Protestant communities. Distinguished from broader Authentic Manhood / Promise Keepers descendants by Evans's specific Black-evangelical voice and Dallas-based platform.

entries.name: Kiwanis International
entries.description: International civic service organization founded in 1915 in Detroit. Operates clubs across the US, Canada, and worldwide focused on community service especially for children. Programs include Key Club (high school) and Builders Club (middle school) youth-development partnerships. Co-ed since 1987; many local clubs remain male-majority. Smaller absolute footprint than [[Lions Clubs International]] or [[Rotary International]] but distinctive youth-focused civic orientation.

entries.name: Knights of Columbus Canada
entries.description: Canadian membership of the [[Knights of Columbus]] — among the largest national jurisdictions of KofC outside the US, with approximately 250,000 Canadian members and 1,700 councils. KofC arrived in Canada in 1897 (Montreal); subsequent Canadian growth was strongest in Quebec (where it is known as "Chevaliers de Colomb") and in Ontario, Atlantic Canada, and the Prairie provinces. Members are practicing Catholic men.

entries.name: Knights of Columbus
entries.description: Catholic fraternal order with thousands of local councils across the US providing fellowship, charitable work, and faith formation for Catholic men 18 and over. Membership requires being a practicing Catholic man; council activity is typically monthly with charitable and family-focused programming. Long-running and accessible to its target population — not a low-barrier door for non-Catholics.

entries.name: Knights of Da Gama
entries.description: South African Catholic lay men's fraternal order, founded 1923 to support Catholic men in faith, family, and public life. Named after the Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama, who is associated with Catholic mission in southern Africa. Operates councils across South Africa with monthly meetings, supporting Catholic charitable, social-justice, and faith-formation activities. Membership requires being a practising Catholic man.

entries.name: Knights of Lithuania
entries.description: Lithuanian-American Catholic fraternal organization founded in 1913. Membership open to Catholics of Lithuanian descent. Operates councils across the US in cities with substantial Lithuanian-American Catholic populations — Chicago (largest US Lithuanian community), Boston, NYC, Detroit, Philadelphia, Cleveland. Programs include Lithuanian cultural preservation, charitable work, and Catholic faith formation.

entries.name: Knights of Peter Claver
entries.description: African-American Catholic fraternal order, founded in 1909 in Mobile, AL, named for Saint Peter Claver who ministered to enslaved Africans in Cartagena. Local councils across the US provide fellowship, charitable work, and faith formation for Black Catholic men. Functionally parallel to [[Knights of Columbus]] but historically founded because Black men were often excluded from KofC councils in the segregated South. Active in dioceses with significant Black Catholic populations (Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi, Alabama, Maryland, and urban centers).

entries.name: Knights of Pythias
entries.description: Fraternal order founded in 1864 in Washington, DC by Justus H. Rathbone, the first fraternal order chartered by Act of Congress. Operates lodges across the US — diminished from its 19th-century peak but still active. Motto is "Friendship, Charity, Benevolence." Membership requires belief in a Supreme Being. The Pythian Sisters is a parallel organization. Smaller national footprint than [[Freemasonry]] or [[BPOE Elks]] today.

entries.name: Knights of St Columba (Scotland)
entries.description: Scottish Catholic fraternal order, founded in 1919 in Glasgow. Operates councils across Scotland providing fellowship, charitable work, and Catholic faith formation. Distinct from the Irish [[Knights of St Columbanus]] (1915 Belfast) and from the US/Canada [[Knights of Columbus]] / [[Knights of Columbus Canada]].

entries.name: Knights of St Columbanus
entries.description: Irish Catholic fraternal order, founded in 1915 in Belfast (now headquartered in Dublin). Approximately 3,000 members across the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland. Programs include charitable work, Catholic social teaching, and fellowship. The Irish counterpart to [[Knights of Columbus]] (US/Canada Catholic fraternal) — distinct organization with its own structure and history.

entries.name: Knights of St. John (Catholic)
entries.description: Catholic men's fraternal organization with military-uniform regalia, founded in 1879 by German-American immigrants. Operates commanderies across the US in cities with historical German Catholic populations. Programs include charitable work, ceremonial honor-guard service at Catholic events, and Catholic faith formation. Smaller in absolute size than [[Knights of Columbus]] but distinctive for its military-style structure and regalia.

entries.name: Knights of the Southern Cross
entries.description: Australian Catholic lay men's fraternal order, founded in Melbourne in 1919 to support Catholic men in faith, family, and public life. Operates state-based provinces with local branches that meet typically monthly, supporting Catholic charitable, social-justice, and faith-formation activities.
