entries.name: Sterling Men's Weekend
entries.description: Personal-development weekend retreat for men, run by the Sterling Institute of Relationship since the early 1980s. Weekend format combines confrontational group work, exercises, and brotherhood building, with ongoing "men's teams" that continue meeting after the weekend. Historically active in California and other West Coast metros, with periodic regional events elsewhere.

entries.name: Sunshine Coast Health Centre
entries.description: British Columbia residential addiction-treatment centre on the Sunshine Coast (Powell River area), founded in 2004, with a specifically men-only clinical model. Combines 12-step rooted recovery with non-12-step elements (CBT, motivational interviewing, recreation therapy). Insurance-funded for many participants; private-pay also.

entries.name: Tablighi Jamaat
entries.description: Global Sunni Muslim revivalist movement founded 1926 in Mewat, India, by Maulana Muhammad Ilyas al-Kandhlawi. Tablighi Jamaat ("Society for Spreading Faith") is one of the largest grassroots Islamic movements in the world, with active presence across 150+ countries. Distinctively organised around weekly mosque-based gatherings (mashwara), longer-form daawah excursions (khuruj — typically 3 days, 40 days, or 4 months), and an annual ijtema (mass-gathering — the Bishwa Ijtema in Bangladesh and the Raiwind Ijtema in Pakistan are among the largest annual male-religious gatherings on earth, drawing millions). Men-only by traditional structure (women's separate Tablighi work exists in some contexts). Free participation; entirely volunteer-led, no formal hierarchy. Operates through local mosque networks rather than a central headquarters.

entries.name: Team Rubicon
entries.description: Veteran-led disaster response organization founded in 2010 after the Haiti earthquake. Deploys teams of military veterans (called "Greyshirts") plus civilian volunteers to disaster-response operations across the US and internationally — hurricanes, wildfires, floods, tornadoes. Operations include initial damage assessment, debris removal, mucking-and-gutting, and longer-term rebuild coordination. Free for participating veterans; training provided.

entries.name: The American Legion
entries.description: Fraternal organization for US military veterans, founded in 1919. Membership is open to any honorably discharged US veteran (no foreign-service requirement, unlike [[Veterans of Foreign Wars]]). Operates roughly 12,000 local posts across the US providing fellowship, veteran advocacy, youth programs (Boys State, American Legion Baseball), and community service. Larger and broader than VFW; the most accessible veterans' fraternal in the country in terms of intake.

entries.name: The Bowery Mission
entries.description: Christian mission to homeless and unhoused men in New York City, founded in 1879. Operates a Men's Center on the Bowery with a residential discipleship/recovery program (typically 9–12 months) integrating addiction recovery, vocational training, and Christian formation. Free for participants; supported by donor philanthropy. One of the oldest continuously-operating rescue missions in the US.

entries.name: The Bridge to Recovery
entries.description: Residential therapy and addiction-recovery center in Bowling Green, KY, founded in 1981. Uses a 14-day workshop format combining group therapy, addiction recovery, and trauma work. Smaller and less well-known than [[The Meadows]] or [[Hazelden Betty Ford]] but with a distinct workshop-intensive model focused on emotional and trauma recovery.

entries.name: The Center for Group Studies
entries.description: NYC-based group-analysis training institute and clinical practice, founded in 1979 by Louis Ormont. Offers ongoing therapy groups including men's-focused groups, plus training programs for clinicians who want to lead group therapy. The most-established academic group-therapy practice in NYC — direct service is geographically limited to the metro area, but the Ormont-method approach has shaped clinicians nationwide.

entries.name: The Character Company
entries.description: South African mentoring charity matching boys (typically aged 7–16) without active father figures with screened, trained adult-male mentors for long-term group and one-to-one mentoring. Founded 2011, based in Johannesburg with chapters across Gauteng and other provinces. Vetted intake — both boys and mentors are screened and oriented. Free for the boys and their families.

entries.name: The Doe Fund
entries.description: NYC-based non-profit founded in 1985 by George T. McDonald, providing transitional work, paid training, supportive housing, and case management for homeless and formerly-incarcerated men. The "Ready, Willing & Able" program is the Doe Fund's signature — distinctive blue uniforms, daily street-cleaning work, and a structured 9–12 month residential program with substance-use treatment, GED prep, and job placement.

entries.name: The Father Effect
entries.description: Christian-rooted fatherhood ministry founded by John Finch around the 2014 documentary film of the same name. Programs address the impact of fatherlessness and the work of becoming a present, healing father. Includes a short documentary, a workbook curriculum for small groups, and ongoing speaking and church-based programming.

entries.name: The Hoffman Institute
entries.description: Personal-development non-profit running "The Hoffman Process" — a week-long residential intensive addressing patterns from childhood and the dysfunctional behaviors that grow out of them, founded in 1967 by Bob Hoffman. Group size is intentionally small (around 30 participants per cohort); held at retreat properties in California and selected international locations. Mixed-gender, but the structured emotional work creates substantial men's-gathering function for participating men, and many participate as a pre-requisite to longer therapy or men's-work paths.

entries.name: The Junto Institute
entries.description: Chicago-based leadership-development and peer-circle organization for founders, CEOs, and emerging leaders, founded in 2014 in the lineage of Benjamin Franklin's original Junto discussion circles. Programs combine teaching, peer feedback, and small-group reflection in a Franklin-style "junto" format. Cohorts run one to two years; alumni network continues afterward. Mixed-gender in many cohorts but functions as significant men's-gathering for participating men.

entries.name: The Last Mile
entries.description: In-prison technology and entrepreneurship training program for incarcerated men and women, founded in 2010 at San Quentin State Prison. Participants learn coding, web development, audio/video production, and other technical skills in a structured classroom environment, plus business mentorship from outside professionals. Alumni network supports re-entry employment and continued growth.

entries.name: The Man Cave
entries.description: Australian charity running preventative mental-health and emotional-development programs for adolescent boys (typically Years 8–10) in schools and community settings. Founded in 2014. Programs are facilitated by trained men and use a mix of group dialogue, storytelling, and rites-of-passage framing to support boys through adolescence with stronger emotional vocabulary, healthier relationships, and clearer identity formation. Operates across multiple Australian states with school partnerships.

entries.name: The Meadows
entries.description: Residential addiction and trauma treatment center in Wickenburg, AZ, founded in 1976. Distinctive for its integration of trauma work (Pia Mellody's developmental immaturity model) with traditional addiction treatment. Mixed-gender residential program plus specialized programs (The Meadows Outpatient, Willow House for women, Brookside Place for chemical dependency, Rio Retreat Center for workshops).

entries.name: The Men's Project (Jesuit Social Services)
entries.description: Healthy-masculinity research-and-program initiative within Jesuit Social Services, the social-justice arm of the Australian Jesuits. Best known internationally for *The Man Box* study (2017, repeated 2024), which measured the prevalence of rigid masculine norms among Australian men and their correlation with violence, depression, and suicide. The Men's Project also runs Modelling Respect & Equality (MoRE), Unpacking the Man Box workshops, and partnerships with sports clubs, schools, and workplaces.

entries.name: The Mission Continues
entries.description: Non-profit founded in 2007 deploying post-9/11 veterans into community service in underserved neighborhoods through "Service Platoons" — local teams of veterans who commit to ongoing volunteer service projects together. Operates in cities across the US. Free for participating veterans. Distinct from purely-fraternal VSOs by its explicit civilian-service mission as a vehicle for veteran reintegration and continued purpose.

entries.name: The Mosque Cares (Imam W. Deen Mohammed Community)
entries.description: Network of Sunni Muslim mosques and communities established by Imam Warith Deen Mohammed (1933–2008), son of Elijah Muhammad. After his father's death in 1975, W. Deen Mohammed led the largest movement of African-American Muslims into mainstream Sunni Islam, transforming the Nation of Islam infrastructure he inherited. The Mosque Cares maintains his legacy and the affiliated mosque network. Active in major US metros with substantial Black American Muslim populations.

entries.name: The Mountaineers
entries.description: Pacific Northwest outdoor community founded in Seattle in 1906, offering courses and trips in hiking, climbing, mountaineering, paddling, and conservation. Membership-based with seven WA branches plus partner relationships outside the region. Not formally men's-only, but the climbing and mountaineering programs have historically been male-dominated and continue to function for many men as a primary brotherhood — long expedition partnerships, course cohorts, and committee work create durable men-to-men relationships.

entries.name: The Mussar Institute
entries.description: Jewish character-development organization founded in 2004 by Alan Morinis, reviving the 19th-century Eastern European Mussar tradition for contemporary practice. The Mussar tradition emphasizes systematic work on personal character traits (middot) — patience, humility, generosity, equanimity, etc. — through practice, study, and small-group accountability. Offers online courses, in-person retreats, and supports the formation of local "vaad" or chavurot (small accountability groups), some men's-only.

entries.name: The Phoenix
entries.description: Sober active community founded in 2006 in Denver, CO by Scott Strode. Combines fitness (CrossFit-style workouts, hiking, climbing, yoga, cycling) with peer-support recovery community. Free for members with at least 48 hours of continuous sobriety. Operates in cities across the US plus a robust online community.

entries.name: The Stoic Fellowship
entries.description: Modern Stoic practice umbrella organization, founded around 2015, supporting the formation of local "Stoa" — small practice circles — across the US and internationally. Stoic practice involves daily reflection on virtue (wisdom, courage, justice, temperance) drawing on classical Stoic philosophers (Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, Seneca). Mixed-gender by design; many local Stoa skew male, particularly in cities with active modern-Stoic communities (Philadelphia, NYC, San Francisco).

entries.name: The Strenuous Life (Jocko Willink)
entries.description: Online and in-person community for discipline-focused personal development, founded by Jocko Willink (former Navy SEAL, *Extreme Ownership* author) and the Origin USA / Echelon Front team around 2018. Members complete a curriculum of physical and personal-development challenges plus participate in regional in-person events. Audience skews militaristically-disciplined and entrepreneurial.

entries.name: Together We Can (Vancouver)
entries.description: BC-based men's recovery community founded in 1991 in Vancouver, with residential, day-program, and continuing-care services for substance-use issues. One of the larger Canadian men's-specific recovery communities, with a strong alumni and peer-support network.

entries.name: Tomorrow Man
entries.description: Australian social-enterprise running emotional-skills and healthy-masculinity workshops for men and adolescent boys in schools, workplaces, sports clubs, and community settings. Founded in 2017. Programs are typically half- or full-day facilitated workshops focused on practical emotional vocabulary, friendship, vulnerability, and resilience — pitched specifically to "regular blokes" rather than men already in the work. A sister program, Tomorrow Woman, runs in parallel.

entries.name: Top Blokes Foundation
entries.description: Australian mentoring charity running structured small-group mentoring programs for boys and young men aged 10–24, in schools and community settings. Founded in 2006. Programs run as facilitated weekly sessions over a school term, focusing on healthy relationships, mental health, identity, and decision-making. Free for participants; funded through philanthropy, corporate, and government partnerships.

entries.name: Trail Life USA
entries.description: Christian boys' outdoor and character-development program, founded in 2013 as an alternative to Boy Scouts of America following BSA's membership-policy changes. Combines outdoor skills (camping, navigation, service) with explicitly Christian formation. Boys ages 5–18 join age-graded "troops" led by adult male volunteers; the adult-leadership structure ("Trailmen") includes its own training and brotherhood gatherings, making this a real men's-gathering site even though the boys are the ostensible focus. Operates in roughly 1,000 troops across all 50 US states.

entries.name: Trout Unlimited Canada
entries.description: Canadian coldwater fisheries conservation nonprofit founded in 1972 in Calgary, with chapters across Canada. Canadian counterpart to [[Trout Unlimited]] (US) with distinct Canadian governance and conservation focus on Atlantic salmon, native trout populations, and Pacific salmon recovery. Chapter events provide fly-fishing fellowship and habitat-restoration days.

entries.name: Trout Unlimited
entries.description: Coldwater fisheries conservation organization founded in 1959 in Michigan, with approximately 400 chapters across the US. Members participate in stream restoration, advocacy for clean watersheds, and chapter fly-fishing events. Officially mixed-gender; many local chapter events function as significant men's-gathering sites in regions where fly fishing remains male-coded.

entries.name: Tungasuvvingat Inuit (TI)
entries.description: Ottawa-based urban Inuit service organization, founded in 1987. Provides culturally-rooted social services, mental-health programming, employment support, and community wellness for Inuit living in southern Canada (especially the Ottawa area). Men's programming includes circles, fatherhood support, traditional teachings, and connection-to-cultural-identity work for Inuit men away from northern home communities.

entries.name: United Church of Christ Men (UCC Men)
entries.description: Men's network of the United Church of Christ (UCC), a mainline Protestant denomination formed in 1957 by the merger of the Congregational Christian Churches and the Evangelical and Reformed Church. UCC is among the most theologically progressive of mainline Protestant denominations, with strong social-justice orientation. Local UCC Men chapters at member congregations run study, retreats, and service projects.

entries.name: UK Men's Sheds Association
entries.description: UK federation of approximately 700 local "Sheds" — community workshops where men gather to make and build things, plus share tea, conversation, and informal support. Australian movement origin (early 2000s); UK chapter founded in 2013. Sheds are typically free or low-cost, operate weekly, and are particularly meaningful for men in retirement, isolation, or post-bereavement.

entries.name: United Church of Canada Men's Network
entries.description: Men's network of the United Church of Canada — the largest Canadian Protestant denomination, formed in 1925 by the merger of Methodist, Congregational, and most Presbyterian congregations in Canada. Theologically progressive mainline, with strong social-justice orientation. Local UCC men's groups at member congregations run study, retreats, and service projects.

entries.name: United Grand Lodge of England (Freemasonry, England + Wales)
entries.description: The oldest Masonic Grand Lodge in the world, founded in 1717. Governs Freemasonry in England and Wales (with separate Grand Lodges for Scotland and Ireland). Approximately 150,000 UK Masons across 6,500 lodges. Membership requires belief in a Supreme Being and is restricted to men in UGLE jurisdiction (the Order of Women Freemasons and HFAF operate parallel jurisdictions for women).

entries.name: United Methodist Men
entries.description: General Commission on United Methodist Men, the men's ministry of the United Methodist Church, founded in 1948. Local chapters at member UMC congregations operate study groups, service projects, men's prayer breakfasts, and the long-running "Strength for Service" daily-devotional ministry distributed to military and first responders. Active across most US states with thousands of chartered chapters.

entries.name: Unitarian Universalist Men's Network (UUMeN)
entries.description: Men's network within the Unitarian Universalist Association — a religiously pluralist denomination that draws from Judeo-Christian, humanist, Buddhist, pagan, and other traditions. UUMeN organizes biennial men's conferences and supports local UU congregational men's groups. UU theology is non-dogmatic by design; the men's network reflects this with broad latitude in spiritual orientation.

entries.name: Vedanta Society
entries.description: Hindu spiritual tradition (Advaita Vedanta) brought to the US by Swami Vivekananda starting at the 1893 Parliament of the World's Religions. Approximately 13 Vedanta Society centers across the US (NY, San Francisco, LA, Boston, Chicago, Portland OR, Seattle, St. Louis, Sacramento, Berkeley, Hollywood, etc.). Each center is led by a sannyasi (Hindu monk) of the Ramakrishna Order and offers public lectures, meditation classes, scripture study, and study circles. Mixed-gender; men's-specific gathering happens through participation.

entries.name: Veterans Expeditions
entries.description: Non-profit running peer-led wilderness expeditions for US military veterans, founded in 2010. Expeditions include backpacking, mountaineering, climbing, and skiing trips of varying length and skill level, designed to provide brotherhood, post-service purpose, and trauma processing in wilderness settings. Veteran-led; participants are veterans of all eras.

entries.name: Veterans of Foreign Wars
entries.description: Fraternal organization for US military veterans with overseas or hostile-fire-zone service, founded in 1899. Operates roughly 6,000 local posts across the US providing fellowship, advocacy, suicide-prevention support, and community service. Membership requires verified foreign or combat service. Posts meet monthly with charitable, social, and policy programming, and many posts host bar/canteen spaces that double as informal gathering points.

entries.name: Vineyard USA Men's Ministry
entries.description: Men's ministry of Vineyard USA, the US affiliate of the Vineyard Movement — an evangelical-charismatic Protestant denomination founded in 1974 by John Wimber. Approximately 500 US Vineyard churches; men's programming varies by congregation, typically including study groups, retreats, and service. Distinctive theological position combines evangelical Protestantism with charismatic gifts, centering "naturally supernatural" Christian practice.

entries.name: Vishva Hindu Parishad of America (VHPA)
entries.description: Hindu cultural and civic organization in the US, founded in 1970 as the American chapter of the Vishva Hindu Parishad. Programs include Hindu cultural events, youth education (Bal Vihar / Bal Sanskar), interfaith dialogue, and community service. Active in major US metros with significant Hindu populations — particularly NJ, CA, NY, IL, TX. Distinct from temple-based gathering ([[BAPS Swaminarayan]]) by its more general Hindu-civic-cultural orientation.

entries.name: Volunteers of America (VOA)
entries.description: National Christian human-services nonprofit founded in 1896 by Ballington and Maud Booth (originally an offshoot of The Salvation Army). Operates programs across the US including reentry and rehabilitation services, addiction recovery, transitional and supportive housing, services for veterans, and behavioral health programs. Many VOA programs include men's-specific residential and group structures.

entries.name: Wabano Centre for Aboriginal Health
entries.description: Ottawa-based urban Indigenous health and wellness centre serving First Nations, Inuit, and Métis people in the National Capital Region, founded in 1998. Programs include men's-specific wellness circles, fatherhood support, traditional teachings, mental-health services, and primary health care. Free for Indigenous community members. One of the major urban Indigenous health centres in Canada.

entries.name: White Bison / Wellbriety Movement
entries.description: Native American recovery community founded in 1988 by Don Coyhis (Mohican Nation), with national headquarters in Colorado Springs. The Wellbriety Movement adapts 12-step recovery through indigenous cultural lenses — talking circles, the Medicine Wheel, the Four Laws of Change, and the integration of traditional Native spirituality. Open to all (not Native-only) but rooted in Native American practice and led by Native facilitators. Free, peer-led, with both in-person and online meetings.

entries.name: Wild at Heart Boot Camps
entries.description: Multi-day Christian men's retreats based on John Eldredge's 2001 book *Wild at Heart* and his ongoing ministry, Ransomed Heart. Boot camps combine teaching, outdoor settings, small-group sharing, and ritual aimed at recovering what Eldredge calls "the masculine heart" within an evangelical Christian frame. Held several times a year at retreat properties (primarily in Colorado) plus occasional regional events; ongoing local "Wild at Heart" small groups operate between camps.

entries.name: Wounded Warrior Project
entries.description: Veterans service organization founded in 2003 specifically for post-9/11 veterans wounded in combat. Programs include peer-support groups (Project Odyssey for combat-stress recovery), mental-health services, adaptive sports, employment support, and family programs. Free for registered Wounded Warriors and their families.

entries.name: Yale Senior Societies
entries.description: Cluster of Yale University senior societies (Skull and Bones, founded 1832; Scroll and Key, 1842; Wolf's Head, 1883; Berzelius; Book and Snake; Elihu; Manuscript; Mace and Chain; St. Elmo; and others) that select graduating-junior students through "Tap Day" each spring and bring them into year-long meetings during senior year. Most are now co-ed but were historically men-only, and continue to function as durable elite-network gathering forms with continuing alumni traditions. Listed for completeness; not a directory pathway for most users.

entries.name: Yiriman Project
entries.description: Aboriginal-led intergenerational youth-on-country programme based in the Kimberley region of Western Australia, founded 2000. Yiriman ("the journey of returning home") takes Aboriginal young people (with focus on at-risk young men) on extended bush trips with cultural elders from Karajarri, Mangala, Nyikina, and Walmajarri country. Trips combine traditional law-and-culture transmission with practical land-management, hunting, fishing, and storytelling. A recognised model in Australian Aboriginal youth-justice and cultural-revitalisation programming. Operates under the Kimberley Aboriginal Law and Culture Centre (KALACC). Funded primarily by Australian government grants. Vetted intake (referral via family / community / juvenile justice).

entries.name: YMCA Adventure Guides
entries.description: Father-child outdoor and family-bonding program operated through participating YMCAs across the US. Activities include monthly tribe meetings, weekend campouts, and longer summer camps. Fathers and their children (typically ages 5–9) work through age-graded programs together. The program was previously known as Y-Indian Guides and was rebranded due to cultural-appropriation concerns about its original Native American framing.
